title: The neuroanatomy lab
intro: Brains in the lab today: plastinated specimens on every table, sliced in three planes, and a set of colored models you can take apart.

steps.say: "Gloves on. Hold the brain in both hands, like something precious, because it is. Start with the ventricles: the brain is built around them."
steps.speaker: Dr. Helen Marsh, Course Director

steps.say: You turn the brain over in your hands: the frontal lobe, the lateral sulcus, the gyri on either side of the central sulcus.

steps.question: neuro_broca_01
steps.lead: "Find the inferior frontal gyrus. What lives there?"

steps.say: Underneath: the circle of arteries at the base of the brain, and the nerves leaving the brainstem like the strings of an instrument.

steps.question: neuro_cn3_01
steps.lead: Dr. Marsh points her probe between two small arteries.

steps.say: "Next week, the spinal cord. And some of you will be neurologists, and one day you'll hold a reflex hammer and remember this afternoon."
steps.speaker: Dr. Helen Marsh, Course Director

feedback: "You could teach this lab next year."
"Good. Walk through the ventricles again with the models before the exam."
"Spend an hour with the brain models in the library's anatomy room."
